findings.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90`

**Raises on non-members.** Rails' `CollectionAssociation#delete` converts integer arguments via `find(records)`, scoped to the association. `group.users.delete(42)` where user 42 is not in the group raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` → error response instead of a no-op. The deleted spec `"succeeds silently when removing non-members"` documented this as intended behavior. Also reachable via `params.require(:user_id).to_i` on a non-numeric value (`"abc".to_i == 0` → `delete(0)` → not found).

*Failure scenario:* admin double-clicks the remove "×" on a member. First request removes them; second returns 404. Because `Group#removeMember` in `group.js:45` has no rejection handler, the member list is never refreshed and the row stays on screen — the UI looks broken.

**Skips join-model callbacks.** For `has_many :through` with no `:dependent` option, `delete` uses the `:delete_all` strategy — it issues `DELETE FROM group_users ...` directly and never instantiates `GroupUser`. If `GroupUser` declares `belongs_to :group, counter_cache: "user_count"` (which the `groups.user_count` column, `BasicGroupSerializer`, and the admin group list all imply — please verify against the model, which isn't in this tree), then **adds increment `user_count` but removes never decrement it**. `add_members` correctly uses `group.add(user)`, so the drift is one-directional and permanent until `refresh_automatic_groups!` runs. The admin edit page hides this because it re-reads `meta.total` (a live `COUNT`), but the group *index* reads the stale column.
`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-23`

`GET /groups/trust_level_0/members.json?limit=99999999` — serializes the entire user table through `GroupUserSerializer` in one unauthenticated request. Memory/CPU DoS plus wholesale user enumeration.
`?offset=-1` or `?limit=-1` — PostgreSQL raises `OFFSET must not be negative` / `LIMIT must not be negative` → 500 from an unauthenticated GET.
`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:23-25`

The client's `asJSON()` (`group.js:63-69`) sends `name`, `alias_level`, and `visible` on both create and update, but `create` only reads `name` and `visible`. `update` reads `alias_level`. So an admin who picks "Everyone" in the alias combo-box on the new-group form gets a group saved with the default level — and the client model keeps the chosen value locally, so the UI displays the wrong state until reload. (Pre-existing, but `create` was rewritten here and the unified form makes it more reachable.)
`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:45,56`; `admin-group.js.es6:56,64`

`removeMember` and `addMembers` attach only a success handler. Every failure path — 422 automatic-group, 400 from `params.require`, network error — is swallowed as an unhandled rejection with zero UI feedback. This is inconsistent with `save` and `destroy` in the same controller, which both `bootbox.alert` on failure. Compounding it, the server *silently skips* usernames that don't resolve (`admin/groups_controller.rb:72`), so a typo'd username just vanishes with no indication.

**No spec at all for the rewritten `GroupsController#members`** — the headline pagination change (limit, offset, `meta` envelope, response-shape change) is entirely untested. There's no `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` in the diff.
The deleted `"succeeds silently when removing non-members"` test is precisely the case that issue #1 now breaks. Deleting the test that would have caught the regression is the wrong direction.
The deleted `"succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"` coverage is also gone, though the behavior is retained in code.
Renaming a *non-automatic* group is now untested (that path went away with `"is able to update group members"`). Only the negative case at line 51 remains.

Line 115: `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` uses PUT against a route that only accepts DELETE (line 125 in the same file correctly uses `:delete`). Controller specs dispatch the action directly so it passes, but it documents the wrong verb.
Lines 52, 94, 115 hardcode `id: 1` / `group_id: 1`, relying on seed data for an automatic group, while the rest of the file uses `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`. Inconsistent and brittle.
Line 53's assertion `group.name.should_not == "WAT"` is weak — it doesn't verify the name is *unchanged*.
`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28`, `config/routes.rb:49-50`, `admin/groups_controller.rb:23,32`
`GET /groups/:name/members` response shape: bare array → `{ members: [...], meta: {...} }`. Any plugin, mobile client, or API consumer breaks.
`POST /admin/groups` and `PUT /admin/groups/:id` payload: nested `group[name]` → flat `name`.
`PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes: { add:, delete: }` is removed outright. That endpoint's shape strongly suggests it was built for external/plugin use.

**`admin-group.js.es6:62` — `// TODO: should clear the input` shipped as-is.** `usernames` is never reset after a successful add, so the selector keeps the text and clicking "Add" again re-submits the same list. Small, but it's a visible rough edge in the feature this PR is named after.

**`admin/groups_controller.rb:77,92` — `if group.save` is dead error handling.** Both `group.add(user)` (push on a persisted `has_many`) and `users.delete` write immediately; `save` on an otherwise-unchanged persisted record returns `true`, so `render_json_error(group)` is unreachable. It reads like errors are handled when they aren't.

**`admin/groups_controller.rb:71` — `usernames.split(",")` assumes a String.** `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` yields an Array → `NoMethodError` → 500. No `.strip` per username, so `"a, b"` silently drops `b`. No cap on list length, so a large paste is an unbounded N-query + N-insert request.

**`group.js:21` — `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`** returns `undefined` where the previous code returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. No current caller chains off it, but `removeMember`/`addMembers` and both routes call it, so any future `.then()` throws. Also the stray space in `return ;`.
**`group.js:70` — instance method named `create`** on an `Ember.Object` subclass is confusing next to the class-level `Discourse.Group.create()`. `saveNew` or similar would be clearer.
**`admin-group.js.es6:17` — `Discourse.computed.propertyEqual` global** used inside an ES6 module; the convention elsewhere is `import { propertyEqual } from 'discourse/lib/computed';`.
**Four `!important` declarations** in the new `.groups` SCSS block (`admin_base.scss:465,468,473,475`) — specificity workaround worth resolving properly.

**`routes.rb:49` — non-RESTful.** `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members` with `user_id` in the body would be more idiomatic as `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members/:user_id`; `put "members"` for *adding* would be more idiomatic as `POST`.
**`admin-group.js.es6:29,40` — no in-flight guard** on next/previous; rapid clicks fire concurrent requests and the last response to land wins arbitrarily.

**`group/members.hbs:1` — `{{#if model}}`** is now always true (model is the Group, not the members array), so an empty group renders a bare table with a "Last seen" header and no rows. The implicit empty-state is gone.

**Whitespace-only churn** in `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs`, `admin-group-selector.hbs`, and the `protected` method re-indentation in both controllers inflates the diff for no functional reason.
**Missing semicolon** after `group.js:59` `})` (ASI covers it), and a stray `;` after the block at `group.js:80`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90`

**Raises on non-members.** Rails' `CollectionAssociation#delete` converts integer arguments via `find(records)`, scoped to the association. `group.users.delete(42)` where user 42 is not in the group raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` → error response instead of a no-op. The deleted spec `"succeeds silently when removing non-members"` documented this as intended behavior. Also reachable via `params.require(:user_id).to_i` on a non-numeric value (`"abc".to_i == 0` → `delete(0)` → not found).

adjudication.rationale: The new `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` does `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i` and then calls `group.users.delete(user_id)`. In ActiveRecord, `CollectionAssociation#delete` will call `find(*records)` when given non-model arguments (like an Integer), and `find` is scoped to the association; if that user id is not currently a member of the group, it raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` rather than being a no-op. The diff also removed the prior spec coverage for “succeeds silently when removing non-members”, indicating intended no-op behavior that is no longer guaranteed. Additionally, a non-numeric `user_id` like "abc" becomes `0` via `to_i`, making the not-found/raise path easy to hit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: *Failure scenario:* admin double-clicks the remove "×" on a member. First request removes them; second returns 404. Because `Group#removeMember` in `group.js:45` has no rejection handler, the member list is never refreshed and the row stays on screen — the UI looks broken.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s `remove_member` server endpoint (`Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`) does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then `group.save`, rendering `success_json` on success; deleting a non-member is typically a no-op and would not inherently produce a 404 (and there’s no explicit 404 path shown). On the client, `Group#removeMember` triggers `self.findMembers()` on the first successful DELETE, so even if a second request failed, the list would already have been refreshed by the first request’s `.then(...)`. Therefore the proposed “second returns 404 → list never refreshed → row stays” scenario is not verifiable from this diff and relies on an unsupported assumption about server behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Skips join-model callbacks.** For `has_many :through` with no `:dependent` option, `delete` uses the `:delete_all` strategy — it issues `DELETE FROM group_users ...` directly and never instantiates `GroupUser`. If `GroupUser` declares `belongs_to :group, counter_cache: "user_count"` (which the `groups.user_count` column, `BasicGroupSerializer`, and the admin group list all imply — please verify against the model, which isn't in this tree), then **adds increment `user_count` but removes never decrement it**. `add_members` correctly uses `group.add(user)`, so the drift is one-directional and permanent until `refresh_automatic_groups!` runs. The admin edit page hides this because it re-reads `meta.total` (a live `COUNT`), but the group *index* reads the stale column.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes member removal from the old path that called `group.remove(user)` (which likely destroys a join record via model code) to `group.users.delete(user_id)` in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`. In Rails, `association.delete` on a `has_many :through` removes rows from the join table without instantiating/destroying the join model, so any join-model callbacks/counter-cache updates won’t run. This is especially problematic here because the UI and serializers rely on a persisted `groups.user_count` column (seen throughout the diff: `BasicGroupSerializer` output in specs expects it, admin pagination uses `user_count`, etc.), while the members endpoint now returns a live `COUNT` in `meta.total`, masking drift on the edit page. Even if the exact counter-cache implementation isn’t shown in this diff, the new code clearly bypasses the model-level add/remove mechanisms and can leave the stored `user_count` stale compared to actual membership.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-23`

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` take client-supplied pagination values with no validation/capping. This diff also makes pagination apply to all groups (previously only automatic groups were paginated and had a bounded default), so a request can now pass very large or negative values (e.g., `limit=-1` / huge limit, or `offset=-10`) leading to unbounded queries/large responses or DB errors (negative OFFSET in Postgres), which is a real correctness/performance issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `GET /groups/trust_level_0/members.json?limit=99999999` — serializes the entire user table through `GroupUserSerializer` in one unauthenticated request. Memory/CPU DoS plus wholesale user enumeration.
`?offset=-1` or `?limit=-1` — PostgreSQL raises `OFFSET must not be negative` / `LIMIT must not be negative` → 500 from an unauthenticated GET.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then calls `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. If a client supplies `?offset=-1`, Rails will generate SQL with `OFFSET -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects (`OFFSET must not be negative`), producing a 500. This endpoint is a normal GET and only gated by `guardian.ensure_can_see!`, so for publicly visible groups it can be hit unauthenticated. (The claim about negative `LIMIT` causing the same PostgreSQL error is less certain, but the negative `OFFSET` 500 is verifiable from the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:23-25`

adjudication.rationale: The referenced lines in `Admin::GroupsController#index` simply change the SQL fragment from `"name ilike ?"` to `"name ILIKE ?"` while still using a bound parameter (`where(..., "%#{search}%")`). This does not introduce a correctness or security issue (no SQL injection due to parameter binding; same behavior as before on PostgreSQL). At most it’s a stylistic/cosmetic change in SQL keyword casing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The client's `asJSON()` (`group.js:63-69`) sends `name`, `alias_level`, and `visible` on both create and update, but `create` only reads `name` and `visible`. `update` reads `alias_level`. So an admin who picks "Everyone" in the alias combo-box on the new-group form gets a group saved with the default level — and the client model keeps the chosen value locally, so the UI displays the wrong state until reload. (Pre-existing, but `create` was rewritten here and the unified form makes it more reachable.)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `discourse/models/group.js`, `asJSON()` now returns `{ name, alias_level, visible }`, and `create()` POSTs that object as the request body. But `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` from `params[:name]` and `group.visible` from `params[:visible]` and never reads/sets `params[:alias_level]`. Meanwhile the new admin group form always renders the alias-level combo-box and binds it to `alias_level`, so a user can select e.g. “Everyone” before creating. That chosen `alias_level` will remain on the client model after `create()` (only `id` is updated from the response), even though the server persisted the default alias level. This creates a real persisted-vs-UI mismatch until a reload or a subsequent update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:45,56`; `admin-group.js.es6:56,64`

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a real pagination/offset bug. In `admin-group.js.es6` the `next` action computes `offset = Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`, which can set `offset` equal to `user_count` (e.g., 50 users, limit 50 -> offset becomes 50). In `discourse/models/group.js` `findMembers` then clamps with `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`, still allowing `offset == user_count`, and sends that to `/groups/:name/members.json`. An offset equal to total yields an empty page, so clicking next can blank the member list. This is made worse by `totalPages` being computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (50/50 => 2 pages), so `showingLast` won’t prevent the invalid next-page navigation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `removeMember` and `addMembers` attach only a success handler. Every failure path — 422 automatic-group, 400 from `params.require`, network error — is swallowed as an unhandled rejection with zero UI feedback. This is inconsistent with `save` and `destroy` in the same controller, which both `bootbox.alert` on failure. Compounding it, the server *silently skips* usernames that don't resolve (`admin/groups_controller.rb:72`), so a typo'd username just vanishes with no indication.

adjudication.rationale: In the admin controller `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` and `removeMember` calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member)` without any `.then/.catch` (or equivalent) to surface failures to the user. In `discourse/models/group.js`, both `addMembers` and `removeMember` return `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)`; if the AJAX call rejects (e.g., 422 from `can_not_modify_automatic`, 400 from `params.require`, network error), that rejection is not handled by the caller, so the UI provides no feedback. Separately, the server-side `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` explicitly ignores unknown usernames (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`), meaning typos are silently dropped with no error returned, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **No spec at all for the rewritten `GroupsController#members`** — the headline pagination change (limit, offset, `meta` envelope, response-shape change) is entirely untested. There's no `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly rewrites `GroupsController#members` to return a different JSON shape (`{members: ..., meta: ...}`) and adds pagination params. However, the finding’s core claim that this change is “entirely untested” is not verifiable from the diff alone: the diff does not show whether `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` (or other specs) already exists and covers `#members` without needing changes. The diff only shows that no new/updated spec for `GroupsController#members` was added here, which is a test-coverage suggestion rather than a concrete defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The deleted `"succeeds silently when removing non-members"` test is precisely the case that issue #1 now breaks. Deleting the test that would have caught the regression is the wrong direction.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the old PATCH-based incremental membership update behavior (including the “removing non-members” case) and replaces it with dedicated endpoints: `remove_member` deletes by `user_id` via `group.users.delete(user_id)`. In Rails/ActiveRecord, deleting a non-associated id is typically a no-op, so the new code still appears to “succeed silently” for non-members. Also, the removed test targeted an API surface (`changes: { delete: ... }` on `update`) that no longer exists, so deleting that test is consistent with the refactor rather than a verifiable regression. The finding relies on an external “issue #1” and is not demonstrably a defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The deleted `"succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"` coverage is also gone, though the behavior is retained in code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the spec example `"succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"` (the whole incremental PATCH update section was deleted) and the new `add_members` implementation still skips unknown usernames (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`), so the behavior appears retained. However, the proposed finding is about lost test coverage rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code. The diff does not demonstrate a runtime problem—only reduced test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Renaming a *non-automatic* group is now untested (that path went away with `"is able to update group members"`). Only the negative case at line 51 remains.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the prior spec that exercised updating a regular (non-automatic) group, including renaming it (previously in `context '.update'` via "is able to update group members" which asserted `group.name == 'fred'`). The new `context ".update"` only tests the negative case that automatic groups ignore name changes. No remaining test in the shown diff covers renaming a non-automatic group via the new `update` params (`name`, `visible`, `alias_level`). This is a verifiable test coverage regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Line 115: `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` uses PUT against a route that only accepts DELETE (line 125 in the same file correctly uses `:delete`). Controller specs dispatch the action directly so it passes, but it documents the wrong verb.
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the test calls `remove_member` with `xhr :put` even though the route is defined to accept DELETE, matching the golden issue about verb mismatch between spec and route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lines 52, 94, 115 hardcode `id: 1` / `group_id: 1`, relying on seed data for an automatic group, while the rest of the file uses `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`. Inconsistent and brittle.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the updated controller spec, several tests use hardcoded `id: 1` / `group_id: 1` to represent an automatic group (e.g. the ".update" test does `Group.find(1)` and expects it to be automatic; ".add_members" does `group_id: 1` and expects 422). Unlike other tests in the same file that create the needed group via `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`, these rely on implicit test seed/default groups having a specific primary key. That makes the spec brittle and environment/ordering-dependent, and the brittleness is directly introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Line 53's assertion `group.name.should_not == "WAT"` is weak — it doesn't verify the name is *unchanged*.

adjudication.rationale: In the added spec `it "ignore name change on automatic group"`, the assertion `group.name.should_not == "WAT"` only checks the name is not the attempted new value, not that it stayed the original automatic group name. This test would still pass if the group name changed to some other unexpected value (or became nil/blank), so it weakly verifies the intended behavior and can mask regressions. This weakness is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28`, `config/routes.rb:49-50`, `admin/groups_controller.rb:23,32`
`GET /groups/:name/members` response shape: bare array → `{ members: [...], meta: {...} }`. Any plugin, mobile client, or API consumer breaks.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which returns a bare JSON array of serialized users) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e. an object with `members` and `meta` keys. The client code was updated to expect `result.members` and `result.meta`, but any existing consumer of `GET /groups/:name/members(.json)` expecting the previous top-level array would break. This is a verifiable backward-incompatible response shape change in a non-admin controller endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `POST /admin/groups` and `PUT /admin/groups/:id` payload: nested `group[name]` → flat `name`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally changes both ends to use flat parameters. The Ember model `asJSON()` now returns `{name, alias_level, visible}` and `create()`/`save()` send that as the AJAX `data`. Correspondingly, `Admin::GroupsController#create` and `#update` now read `params[:name]`, `params[:alias_level]`, and `params[:visible]` (not `params[:group][:...]`). So there is no verifiable client/server payload mismatch introduced in this diff; it’s a coordinated API shape change, not a bug by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes: { add:, delete: }` is removed outright. That endpoint's shape strongly suggests it was built for external/plugin use.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the controller logic that previously handled PATCH requests with a `changes: { add:, delete: }` payload (`update_patch` is deleted and `update` no longer branches on `request.patch?`). Membership changes are now done via new endpoints (`PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`). However, the proposed finding claims this is a problem because it “suggests external/plugin use,” which is speculative and not verifiable from the diff. From the diff alone, this looks like an intentional API change with a replacement, not a clear defect/bug introduced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`admin-group.js.es6:62` — `// TODO: should clear the input` shipped as-is.** `usernames` is never reset after a successful add, so the selector keeps the text and clicking "Add" again re-submits the same list. Small, but it's a visible rough edge in the feature this PR is named after.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the new `addMembers` action explicitly includes `// TODO: should clear the input` and then calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without ever resetting `this.usernames` (e.g., to `null`/`""`) after the request succeeds. Since the `user-selector` is bound as `usernames=usernames` in `group.hbs`, leaving the controller property unchanged will keep the entered usernames in the selector, making it easy to re-submit the same list by clicking "Add" again. There is no code in the diff that clears it on success.
